key_insight: AI can substantially improve weld-joint quality control by automating defect detection, classification, segmentation, and prediction across non-destructive testing data.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, more consistent, and more objective inspection for safety-critical structures in manufacturing, energy, transportation, and shipbuilding.
method: Systematic review of recent literature on AI-based weld inspection
Analysis of machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, and real-time monitoring methods
Comparison across NDT modalities, including defect detection, classification, segmentation, and quality prediction
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that deep learning, object detection/segmentation models, hybrid frameworks, and transfer learning achieve high detection performance across multiple NDT datasets and inspection tasks.
watch_item: Industrial deployment is constrained by limited standardized datasets, class imbalance, domain shift, and the need for explainable, standards-compliant AI.
paper_title: Artificial Intelligence in Quality Control of Welded Joints
